event.wren_heart2.0.text: You're just in time. I'm inventing a drink, and I've run out of people who'll still taste things.
event.wren_heart2.0.why: nervous host pulling the player in, a hint she has been at this all day

event.wren_heart2.1.text: Taste this, [player]. Be honest. ...Not that honest. Medium honest.

event.wren_heart2.2.text: Honest and kind. You pass. Take the juice, and come back when I'm brave enough to cook actual food.
event.wren_heart2.2.why: gives the juice, points at the kitchen scene

event.wren_heart5.0.text: Everyone thinks I love the noise. Glasses, fiddles, Felix arguing with a herring.
event.wren_heart5.0.why: specific saloon noise, sets up the turn

event.wren_heart5.1.text: Truth is, noise is only people, piled up. I like the people. You're one of my favorite piles.
event.wren_heart5.1.why: the confession, warm with the joke last

event.wren_heart5.2.text: Take a bottle for the road, so the road has company. And come back soon. Before the four o'clock quiet.
event.wren_heart5.2.why: gift plus her fear of the empty room as a thread

event.hall_dance.1.text: Look at this room! Full, and the porch is full too. Somebody count the porch. I need a number for the story.
event.hall_dance.1.why: full room, and she is already turning it into a story

event.hall_dance.2.text: [player]. I said I'd open it on the night, and this is the night. First glass is yours. I poured it before the doors.
event.hall_dance.2.why: a promise kept, with the hostess detail

event.hall_dance.6.text: The whole hall takes the chorus. Piper stops playing and sways, and the song goes on without her.
event.hall_dance.6.why: Piper's song the village sings without her, as seen

event.hall_dance.9.text: The roof pool is closed! Six winters of coins, and Tilda picked the right year. I'm demanding a recount.
event.hall_dance.9.why: rivalry joke; six winters matches the running fact

event.hall_dance.12.text: Marcus takes his one dance, and Tilda takes hers beside him. The lamps burn low, and nobody goes home.
event.hall_dance.12.why: two separate dances the engine can show

event.reading_night.3.text: Don't mind me, I only tell stories. Somebody has to write them down. Otherwise I improve them until nobody recognizes them.
event.reading_night.3.why: teller versus writer, her improving habit, works in all three branches

event.past_the_point.wren.text: Don't mind me. I'm only looking. From the point, the sea looks like it starts somewhere else.
event.past_the_point.wren.why: her bag and the sea, after the player said go

event.story_cat.intro.text: Don't move. A cat has chosen your boots. Eight years I've lived here, and it's never once chosen mine.
event.story_cat.intro.why: envy as warmth; her small want

dlg.story.cat.talk.1.text: Tilda calls it Ledger. Juno says Quench. Piper swears it's Sharp. Hazel files it under Index. I say Gossip. It ignores all five equally. Rude.
dlg.story.cat.talk.1.why: the five names, the shipped Gossip joke as callback

dlg.story.cat.talk.2.text: So. You're the one it picked. What do you call it?
dlg.story.cat.talk.2.why: puts the choice on the chosen one

dlg.story.cat.talk.r0.text: Ledger. Tilda will write that on her slate. In ink. With the date.

dlg.story.cat.talk.r1.text: Quench. Juno will make it a brass name tag, and by Friday I'll say she made two.

dlg.story.cat.talk.r2.text: Sharp. Piper will say she was right all along, in a key of her choosing.

dlg.story.cat.talk.r3.text: Something new? Go on, then. ...It purred. It has never purred for me. That's the one.

event.story_cat.after.text: {if choice:cat.ledger}Ledger! Tilda will be unbearable. By tonight, the cat will be doing her books.{else}{if choice:cat.quench}Quench! Juno will want a vote. By tonight, the cat will have won it.{else}{if choice:cat.sharp}Sharp! Piper will write it a song. By tonight, it'll be a waltz.{else}A new name! Nobody will believe me, so by tonight I'll have made it bigger.{/if}{/if}{/if}
event.story_cat.after.why: the story escalates before it is told

event.wren_heart4.setup.text: Don't sit yet. I'm trying something new, and I need a witness. Possibly an accomplice.

event.wren_heart4.prank.text: Quiet, everybody! The worst song ever written, sung by the person who wrote it!
event.wren_heart4.prank.why: the act announced, her own fault

dlg.wren.openmic.0.text: Well? Be honest. A performer needs one honest face in the crowd. Today you're the whole crowd.
dlg.wren.openmic.0.why: the empty-room fear under the joke

dlg.wren.openmic.r0.text: Oh, I could live on that. Do it again. Louder. Pretend the porch is full.

dlg.wren.openmic.r1.text: A heckler! At last, I'm a real act. You're going in the second verse.
dlg.wren.openmic.r1.why: delight at being taken seriously enough to heckle

dlg.wren.openmic.r2.text: Fair. I'd hide too. Come out, though. The second verse is worse, and you'll want to see it.

event.wren_heart6.intro.text: Come into the back. I'm cooking. I hate cooking. You taste, I stir, and we tell nobody it was me.

dlg.wren.kitchen.0.text: It needs one more thing. Pepper, a splash of cider, or do we leave it alone and back away slowly?

dlg.wren.kitchen.r0.text: Brave it is! If I cry, blame the pepper. Officially, it was always the pepper.

dlg.wren.kitchen.r1.text: Cider. Sweet, with a little mischief in it. Like most of my regulars.

dlg.wren.kitchen.r2.text: Plain? You think it's already good? Nobody has ever said that about my cooking. I'm keeping you.
dlg.wren.kitchen.r2.why: praise lands hard on someone who hates cooking

event.wren_heart6.after.text: It goes on the chalkboard Friday. If anyone asks, you made it and I only stood near it.
event.wren_heart6.after.why: the dish reaches her menu; deflection as affection

event.wren_heart8.intro.text: Close the door behind you. No, the other one. Yes. Now sit, and don't let me make a joke.
event.wren_heart8.intro.why: she is guarding herself and says so

dlg.wren.bag.1.text: I came here to rest for one season. That was eight years ago. So tell me. Go, stay, or leave it under there?

dlg.wren.bag.r0.text: Go. Just like that. You say it like it's easy. ...Maybe it is. I'd want a very good map.

dlg.wren.bag.r1.text: Stay. Oh. That's a nicer word than I expected. I'll keep it in the bag, next to the socks.
dlg.wren.bag.r1.why: touched, hides it in a joke

dlg.wren.bag.r2.text: ...You didn't tell me what to do. Everyone has advice for the one behind the bar. You just let me talk.

event.wren_heart8.after.text: There. I said it out loud, and the bag weighs less. Don't tell anyone. This one I won't improve.
event.wren_heart8.after.why: the one story she leaves alone

event.wren_heart10.intro.text: Tonight I'm performing. One song, one listener, and I've already picked. Sit there. Yes, you.

event.wren_heart10.outro.text: {if choice:wren.bag.go}I'm not leaving yet. But the second verse has a map in it, and the map has the sea.{else}{if choice:wren.bag.stay}The chorus was the stay. I sang it twice, in case you missed it.{else}The quiet bit in the middle was yours. You listened once. I wanted to give some quiet back.{/if}{/if}
event.wren_heart10.outro.why: each branch answers the bag choice

event.wren_friend.intro.text: Friday means bingo. Not numbers. Rumors. Sit down and cross something off.

event.wren_friend.doing.text: Square three: Bram said four words. Square four: Bram said none. Both on good authority. Mine.

event.wren_friend.wrap.text: No bingo today. A full card of nonsense, though, and half of it's mine. Bring a rumor next Friday.

event.wren_birthday.intro.text: It's my birthday, so nobody may look surprised. Sit. Be festive. Have a pickle, I saved the good jar.
event.wren_birthday.intro.why: host on her own day; pickles gift

event.wren_courtship.after.text: {if flag:choice.courtship.wren.yes}Walks, then. And poems. You're stuck with me, and I'm stuck with the stool.{else}{if flag:choice.courtship.wren.friends}The best of friends. It's on my chalkboard now, in capital letters.{else}Whenever you like. I'll be on the stage, being patient. It's a new look.{/if}{/if}
event.wren_courtship.after.why: chalkboard is hers, the slate is Tilda's

event.wren_courtship2.intro.text: Sit. Last time you asked me to wait, and I did. I'm very good at waiting now. I still like you. More, actually.
event.wren_courtship2.intro.why: second ask must not repeat the first

event.wren_courtship2.after.text: {if flag:choice.courtship.wren.yes}Walks, then. And poems. You're stuck with me, and I'm stuck with the stool.{else}{if flag:choice.courtship.wren.friends}The best of friends. It's on my chalkboard now, in capital letters.{else}Still waiting, then. I'm getting rather good at it. Don't tell anyone.{/if}{/if}
event.wren_courtship2.after.why: later branch acknowledges a second wait

dlg.wren.courtship.r1.text: Friends. Yes. The best kind. You keep the good stool, and I keep talking too much. I'm relieved. Mostly.
dlg.wren.courtship.r1.why: gracious, with a small honest crack

event.wren_partners.intro.text: Evening, my darling pickle-eater. I wrote you a song. It's terrible. It's mine. Sit and be sung at.

dlg.wren.partners.r2.text: A walk home. Past the store, past Tilda's lamp, past all my old excuses. Lead on.
dlg.wren.partners.r2.why: no bakery exists; Tilda's lamp is a real landmark

event.overheard_wren_piper_3.l3.text: That's the best verse you've ever said out loud. Write it down. In pencil, before I improve it.

event.overheard_wren_piper_4.l1.text: Piper. Next month, you headline. Top of my chalkboard. I bought new chalk.

event.overheard_tilda_wren_2.l2.text: I heard it first. Three days ago. It's grown since.

event.overheard_tilda_wren_3.l2.text: You've earned the good stool, Tilda. Come at seven. Cider's on me.
event.overheard_tilda_wren_3.l2.why: good stool is canon; Tilda reaches the saloon at seven

event.overheard_wren_bram_1.l1.text: Bram! One cider, three words, every night. Today I want a fourth. I've a fish riding on it.
event.overheard_wren_bram_1.l1.why: sets up the Felix bet paid off in Five Words

event.overheard_wren_hazel_1.l3.text: And which one's true? Careful. I'm attached to the forge.

adds.text: That face. Is that a good face? You have a very private face.
adds.why: her nerves, the beat the bible asks for

adds.text: It's the quiet hours I mind. An empty room echoes. I've timed it.
adds.why: the fear under the warmth, said lightly

threads.wren_heart2: Wren has promised to try actual cooking, and she is clearly afraid of it.
threads.wren_heart5: What happens at the saloon in the four o'clock quiet, when the room is empty?
threads.hall_dance: Nobody ever counts the porch, and Wren wants a recount on a pool Tilda won.
threads.reading_night: Wren tells and someone else writes; who writes Wren's stories down?
threads.past_the_point: Wren is standing on the point looking at the sea after the player told her to go.
threads.story_cat: The cat has never chosen Wren's boots, and by tonight her version of the name will have grown.
threads.wren_heart4: Wren keeps promising a second verse that is even worse.
threads.wren_heart6: The dish goes on the chalkboard Friday, credited to the player.
threads.wren_heart8: Wren says this is the one story she will not improve; the bag is still under the bar.
threads.wren_heart10: The song carries the bag choice; the bag itself is still packed.
threads.wren_friend: Next Friday's card, and which of Wren's two Bram rumors is true.
threads.wren_birthday: Wren will retell this birthday for years, improved each time.
threads.wren_courtship: If the player asked to wait, Wren is practicing patience on the stage.
threads.wren_courtship2: Wren has waited twice now and says so lightly.
threads.wren_partners: The song, the dance or the walk; on the walk the bag is finally unpacked.
threads.overheard_wren_piper_1: Piper threatens to take the bridge up a key out of spite.
threads.overheard_wren_piper_2: Wren's one verse is going into Piper's next song.
threads.overheard_wren_piper_3: Piper's wordless soft song, written down in pencil.
threads.overheard_tilda_wren_1: Tilda's ribbon ends up pinned to the good stool.
threads.overheard_tilda_wren_2: Wren's version of the cat story has a pickle in it; Tilda wants it.
threads.overheard_tilda_wren_3: Tilda's slate, waiting while she sits on the good stool.
threads.overheard_wren_bram_1: Wren still needs a fourth word from Bram, and a fish depends on it.
threads.overheard_wren_bram_2: Bram might let Wren read the ending of an unsent letter.
threads.overheard_wren_bram_3: Bram asked Wren not to go far; the bag is still under the bar.
threads.overheard_wren_hazel_1: Hazel has written down every version of Wren's rumors.
threads.overheard_wren_hazel_2: Hazel may read Wren one line, slowly, from the corner stool.
threads.overheard_wren_hazel_3: Who did Hazel read her poem to, and will she read Wren the line?

notes: hall_dance.9: card said 'seven winters'; the running fact is six winters, so I wrote six. Check Tilda/Marcus lines in that scene for the same number.
hall_dance.12: original 'Tilda lets him lead' implied two people dancing together; rewritten as two separate dances the engine shows.
wren_heart4 card has Wren singing her own bad song; the bible's heart 4 has her volunteer the player to introduce Piper. I followed the card's beats; the choice flags still match.
wren_courtship2.intro was a copy of the first ask; rewritten to acknowledge the wait. The shared dlg.wren.courtship.* keys serve both scenes, so they stay neutral.
wren_partners.r2 mentioned a bakery, which does not exist; now Tilda's lamp. overheard_tilda_wren_3 said six o'clock but Tilda reaches the saloon at seven; fixed.
Kept unchanged on purpose: bag n0 and birthday n0 (shipped lines), heart4 bath joke, Bram 'Four words! Four!' scene, Piper overheard 1-2.
